description: Application speed for PCA: API response time/volume/errors (RED) across services, database query latency (app-side plus CouchDB/OpenSearch internals), Spark batch & streaming speed, and Kafka/Ignite lag.

options.content:
# PCA Application Speed

Response time, request volume and error rate for the platform's APIs, database calls, Spark jobs, and consumer lag – the 'why is it slow?' dashboard.

**Sections**
- **API overview (RED)**: per service Request rate, Error rate (5xx), and Duration (p99). Latency is in seconds.
- **Per-service detail**: slowest endpoints and response-code breakdown for Gather and Skylight-AAA, plus other services.
- **Database speed**: app-side call latency (what the services actually experience calling Dgraph/Postgres/Druid) plus CouchDB and OpenSearch exporter internals.
- **Spark**: streaming micro-batch duration & throughput, batch-job execution time & scheduling delay. A *micro-batch* is the group of messages a Spark app pulls from its Kafka topic each trigger and processes together (streamingapp reads the `ignite.contemporary*` topics, latentapp the `ignite.latent*` topics, and alertstream the `alert-events` topic).
- **Sensor Collector persistence**: batch ship time and cache backlog (files/batches) for roadrunner's on-disk persistence service – the collector's end-of-pipe shipping speed to Fedex.
- **Lag**: Kafka consumer-group lag and Ignite ingestion lag.

**Reading latency:** API/DB summaries expose p50/p90/p99 quantiles directly; histograms (sky-topo, foxtrot, alert-service REST, foxtrot-postgres) use `histogram_quantile`. A rising p99 with flat rate = genuine slowdown; rising rate + rising p99 = load-driven. Correlate DB latency spikes with API latency to localise the cause.

**Note:** nginx has no per-route Prometheus metrics (only stub_status), so API timings come from each upstream service. weld exposes request/error counts but no latency; report-service / custom-reports / tenant-orchestrator did not expose confirmable timing metrics (tell me if they do and I'll add them).

panels.description: Total API request rate across the instrumented services (gather, skylight-aaa, stitchit, alert-service), from the summary _count series.
panels.title: API requests /s

panels.description: Highest p99 response time across those services' endpoints right now (seconds). A climbing value is the headline 'APIs are slow' signal – drill into the per-service detail.
panels.title: Worst API p99

panels.description: Largest consumer-group lag across all topics (kafka-exporter). Growing lag = a consumer (streamingapp/latentapp/alert) is falling behind.

panels.description: How many calls/s each service makes to each datastore (summary _count rate). Volume context for the latency above; a surge can drive both DB and API latency.
panels.title: DB – app-side call rate (calls/s)

panels.description: The gesellix couchdb exporter is only exposing couchdb_httpd_up (reachability); CouchDB's _node/_stats require admin auth and the exporter is started without credentials (args: '--couchdb.uri=http://couchdb:5984' only), so no request-rate/latency series exist. 1 = exporter can reach CouchDB, 0/gap = it cannot. TO GET COUCHDB SPEED METRICS: start the couchdbstats exporter with --couchdb.username / --couchdb.password (CouchDB admin), then request_methods/status_codes/latency series appear and I can wire real panels. (couchdb_max_dbs_open comes from a different service, not this exporter.)
panels.title: CouchDB – reachability (detailed stats unavailable)

panels.description: OpenSearch exporter: average search-query time (query_time_seconds / query_total) and search rate. Rising latency affects logging/alert-index queries (Health Clinic, alerting).
panels.title: OpenSearch – avg query latency (s) & search rate

panels.description: A **micro-batch** is the group of messages the app pulls from its Kafka topic each trigger interval and processes together (streamingapp reads the `ignite.contemporary*` topics, latentapp the `ignite.latent*` topics, and alertstream the `alert-events` topic). This panel shows the per-query processing time per batch (spark_queryBatchDuration) for the streaming apps. GOOD: well under the 60s trigger. Rising = the app is slowing/backing up (correlate with its Kafka lag below).
panels.title: Spark – Micro-Batch Duration (per Kafka batch, ms)

panels.description: Rows processed per second (spark_queryProcessingRate) and input rows per micro-batch (spark_queryInputRows) for the streaming apps. A **micro-batch** is the group of messages the app pulls from its Kafka topic each trigger interval and processes together (streamingapp reads the `ignite.contemporary*` topics, latentapp the `ignite.latent*` topics, and alertstream the `alert-events` topic). Drop to 0 with lag rising = the app stalled.
panels.title: Spark – streaming throughput (rows/s)

panels.description: Execution time of scheduled batch jobs (batch_job_processing_time) by granularity/object. Rising times push out aggregation/compaction and delay data availability.
panels.title: Spark – batch job execution time (s)

panels.description: Number of latent batch partitions still queued for processing per job (spark_AccedianLatentBatchPartitionsCount). GOOD: trends down after a burst. BAD: not decreasing = the latent batch tier is falling behind and late data is delayed. (Replaces the earlier scheduling-delay panel, whose metric job_scheduling_delay is only emitted for compaction-delay measurement and is usually empty.)
panels.title: Spark – latent batch backlog (partitions to process)
Sensor Collector – Persistence Service (ship speed & backlog)

panels.description: How long data batches sit in the Sensor Collector's (roadrunner) on-disk persistence cache before being shipped to Fedex (roadrunner_persistence_service_time_to_ship), per collector. This is the collector's end-of-pipe shipping speed. GOOD: low/stable. BAD: rising → roadrunner is ingesting fine but shipping slowly – usually Fedex is slow/overloaded or the data link is degraded (correlate with the Lag panels and the Sensor Connectivity 'Data Ship Latency'). Unit is as reported by roadrunner (ms); if the axis looks off by 1000x it is seconds.
panels.title: Sensor Collector – Persistence Batch Ship Time

panels.description: Data files cached locally and batches waiting to ship from the Sensor Collector (roadrunner) to Fedex (roadrunner_persistence_service_cached_files, _available_batches), summed per collector. GOOD: low/stable near zero. BAD: steadily climbing → the collector is receiving data faster than it can ship it (slow/broken downstream) and is buffering to disk; a growing backlog precedes a full cache and back-pressure. Pair with Batch Ship Time to tell slow-shipping from a hard stop.
panels.title: Sensor Collector – Persistence Cache Backlog (files & batches)

panels.description: Kafka consumer-group lag (kafka-exporter) for every consumer group/topic. Continuously growing lag for a group = that consumer (streamingapp, latentapp, alertStreaming, ignite, gather) is behind and data is delayed. Flat/low is healthy.
panels.title: Kafka – consumer group lag by topic

panels.description: Ignite's consume lag on the Fedex raw topics (ignite_ingestion_lag). Growing = normalization is behind the ingest rate.
panels.title: Ignite – ingestion lag by topic
